subject: [ACTION REQUIRED] AZ1 sustained 5xx + latency spike — remediation & credit request
messages:
From: Mike Carter <ops@syndicatehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Singh <anita.singh@syndicatehealth.com>
Date: 2029-10-05T09:03:12-07:00
Subject: URGENT: Region AZ1 - sustained 5xx and token timeouts

Mina —

We’re seeing a sustained increase in 5xx responses and end-user timeouts hitting our production traffic that routes to AZ1 starting ~08:50 PT. 5xx rate is ~12% for the last 25 minutes and median p50 latency jumped from 120ms to 1.8s. Our customers in the Midwest are reporting failed submissions and API clients are timing out downstream.

Quick facts:
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat (tokenization-heavy flows)
- Time window: ~08:50 PT — ongoing
- Error signature: 502/504 + token cache eviction logs on our side

We’re in a hard production peak and this is user-facing. Please escalate immediately — we need either a routing failover or confirmed mitigation plan in the next 15 minutes. Also need an estimate for credits for the degraded window.

I’ve attached a short trace and a segment of our logs.

—Mike
Mike Carter
VP, Engineering Ops | Syndicate Health
ops@syndicatehealth.com

Attachments: p0_syndicate_trace_20291005.log (text)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Carter <ops@syndicatehealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-10-05T09:06:31-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Region AZ1 - sustained 5xx and token timeouts

Mike — thanks for the heads up and for the traces; sorry for the disruption. I’m escalating to our infra on-call (cc’d) and opening a PagerDuty incident now. Immediate next steps:

1) PagerDuty incident PD-98421 opened and routed to AZ1 on-call. Link: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-98421
2) Engineering will evaluate KV cache pressure and routing flaps; we’ll confirm if a cross-region steer (us-west-2) is recommended.
3) We’ll propose an immediate canary steer for 10% of your traffic off AZ1 within 10–15m if it looks safe; we will not do a global swap without your OK.
4) I will coordinate an exec bridge if we can’t restore to baseline in 30m.

Can you confirm: is Syndicate comfortable with an incremental canary steer to us-west-2? If yes, we’ll run the drain. I’ve attached the short trace (got it) and we’ll upload any additional logs we need.

I’ll follow up within 10 minutes with updates.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0194

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Mike Carter <ops@syndicatehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-10-05T09:11:08-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Region AZ1 - sustained 5xx and token timeouts

Quick engineering summary (AZ1 oncall):

- We’re seeing KV cache thrash on the sequence-heavy endpoints; memory pressure is forcing frequent cache evictions which correlates with higher latency and downstream 502s.
- Simultaneous routing flap detected between AZ1 and the north-virginia border-edge resulting in transient stream re-attach failures.

Immediate mitigations we can enact now:
- Enable a 10% canary steer of Syndicate traffic to us-west-2 (p95 risk: low). This will serve warm KV cache variants and reduce cold-cache penalty.
- Apply a temporary tighter prefix-KV caching TTL for your keyspace to reduce evictions (10–30m window).
- If we see improvement on the canary in 12m, we can increase to 40% and then full redirect with a rolling drain.

Runbook attached: kvcache_runbook_v2.pdf

If Syndicate approves the canary, we’ll coordinate the steer immediately and monitor error rate and latency. If you prefer we can also fail open to a smaller instance type in AZ1 while maintaining traffic — but that’s slower.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Site Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Mike Carter <ops@syndicatehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Singh <anita.singh@syndicatehealth.com>
Date: 2029-10-05T09:18:44-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Region AZ1 - sustained 5xx and token timeouts

Thanks — please proceed with the 10% canary steer to us-west-2 now. We don’t want to risk global swap unless metrics show widening improvement. Please also flag this to your leadership — our execs are on standby and will want a postmortem and credit plan if this lasts more than 30 minutes.

ETA question: if the canary behaves, how long to reach 40% and then full failover?

—Mike

Subject: Re: URGENT: Region AZ1 - sustained 5xx and latency spike — remediation & credit request

Mike / Anita — wanted to close the loop from our side after the incident and next steps:

Summary of actions taken
- 09:20 PT: we triggered a 10% canary steer to us-west-2 and applied the temporary prefix-KV TTL adjustment.
- 09:32 PT: observed p50 latency drop from 1.8s -> 210ms on the canary; 5xx rate on the canary was <0.5%.
- 09:48 PT: increased steer to 40% after stable metrics for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
- 10:05 PT: completed rolling drain to us-west-2; AZ1 error rate returned to baseline by ~10:12 PT.

Next steps / compensation
- We’ll schedule an executive bridge for 16:00 PT today to walk through the timeline and remediation. I’ve invited our Head of Customer Success and yours.
- Redwood will issue a one-time credit for the impacted window. I’ve prepared a draft credit note — please review and sign: https://docusign.com/agreements/CC-98421. The draft covers net credits for the error-window and an SLA adjustment for the month.
- Engineering will publish a technical post-mortem within 48 hours. We’ll include root cause analysis (KV eviction + routing flap) and mitigation plan (KV TTL tuning, routing stability checks, and additional AZ warm capacity).

Attachments: credit_note_template.docx
PagerDuty incident: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-98421
HubSpot record: https://hubspot.com/contacts/companies/7729

Thanks for partnering on the rapid canary authorize; sorry again for the disruption. If you’d like immediate executive contact before the 16:00 bridge, I can loop in our COO.

—Mina
